articles.title: Dollar Hit by Intervention Despite Bullish Macro Factors. Correction or Reversal?
articles.expand: The Dollar fell despite a hawkish Fed vote, rising yields, and rebounding oil — all bullish macro signals — as Japan's estimated $59 billion intervention and reported US-Japan cooperation introduced a policy-risk variable that overrode them. The key question now: is this a temporary correction, or the start of a broader reversal? The post Dollar Hit by Intervention Despite Bullish Macro Factors. articles.title: Barkin: Rate decision still a "close call"
articles.expand: "It's a close call" whether interest rates are high enough. Would not say whether he would have joined the three Fed officials who dissented in favor of a rate hike. Skeptical that the labor market has strengthened meaningfully. Price increases are continuing to move through the economy unevenly. Barkin is sitting on the fence for now and enjoying the view. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

articles.title: German Inflation Climbs To 3-Month High Amid Energy Price Surge
articles.expand: Consumer price inflation in Germany accelerated at a faster than expected pace in July to its strongest in three months as energy prices surged after the government's fuel tax rebate ended and also due to the intensification of the conflict in the Middle East. The inflation shoot up in the biggest euro area economy has raised the speculation regarding an interest rate hike in September.

articles.title: Bank Of England Holds Key Rate In 6-3 MPC Split
articles.expand: The Bank of England maintained its interest rate in a split vote as renewed tensions in the Middle East reignited fears of high inflation becoming persistent. The Monetary Policy Committee, led by Governor Andrew Bailey, voted 6-3 to hold the bank rate at 3.75 percent, which is the lowest rate since June 2023. Previously, the central bank had reduced the rate by 25 basis points each in August.
